papers.title: WakeSentry: real-time awakening detection from single-channel EEG across sleep cohorts and forehead headbands
papers.summary: Developed WakeSentry, a causal single-channel frontal EEG method that detects sleep awakenings in real time using a dedicated awakening module, evaluated on 1,529 PSG nights from five cohorts and 224 headband nights. At 0.5 false awakenings/hour it raised sensitivity from 63.8% to 70.5% on PSG and from 49.8% to 53.9% on headbands versus GSSC, and as a replayed stimulator gate it shortened wake stimulation while staying open for at least 85% of N2 and N3.

papers.title: NED-Net: open-source software for building and refining seizure detectors during rodent EEG experiments
papers.summary: Introduces NED-Net, open-source software that trains and continuously retrains rodent seizure detectors using reviewed candidate events as labels. A detector across cohorts went from mostly-seizure detections with low per-animal recall to, after cohort-specific retraining, convulsive recall of 64% (up from 15%) with at least one reference seizure in every animal.

papers.title: MLE EEG Toolbox: A Personal AI Laboratory Assistant for Literature-Informed and Reproducible M/EEG Research
papers.summary: Introduced MLE EEG Toolbox, a locally deployed AI assistant framework that translates natural-language instructions into researcher-approved M/EEG analysis operations, integrating literature retrieval, parameter guidance, and replayable computational provenance. It reported action-selection accuracies of 85.6% for EEG and 95.5% for MEG, with 142 cross-platform tests showing close numerical agreement and demonstrated spectral, network, decoding, and source analyses on public datasets.

papers.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: Presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG sleep staging using a serpentine dataflow for long temporal convolutions (6.2× and 2.25× fewer memory accesses than output- and weight-stationary dataflows) and hybrid layer-wise dynamic quantization (4.16× model-size reduction). Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, it consumes 0.40 mW with 258× speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor, staying within 0.15% of floating-point 5-class accuracy and 0.51% for N3 sensitivity on MASS-SS3.

papers.title: Adaptive observation-history fusion for EEG-based tracking of PERCLOS-anchored drowsiness.
papers.summary: Evaluated adaptive observation-history fusion for continuous EEG tracking of PERCLOS-anchored drowsiness in SEED-VIG (21 participants, 23 sessions) under strict 21-fold leave-one-subject-out validation, comparing 11 methods including supervised fusion, PPO-based fusion, and neural temporal models. PPO fusion showed no established predictive advantage over supervised Gate-7D (RMSE difference -0.0023, p=0.349), and no PPO-versus-alternative comparison survived Holm correction.

papers.title: Sample size critically shapes the reliability of EEG case-control findings in psychiatry.
papers.summary: Quantified how sample size affects reliability of resting-state EEG case-control comparisons using repeated random subsampling in a 2,874-participant multisite dataset spanning ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, anxiety, learning disorders, and controls. Small samples produced unstable, inflated, highly variable effect sizes, whereas larger samples converged on uniformly small but robust effects, with statistical power rising steeply and false positive rates remaining relatively stable.

papers.title: Disentangling Monitor Hardware Artifacts and Smoothing Lag for Shift-Robust Intraoperative EEG and Hemodynamic Risk Calibration
papers.summary: Developed causal signal-conditioning and shift-robust conformal calibration for intraoperative EEG and hemodynamic risk forecasting across 5,439 anesthesia procedures, blanking impedance artifacts, separating suppression lag, and distinguishing cuff inflations from dropouts. Filter blanking removed 97.9% and 97.6% of false flatline conflicts while preserving 99.2% and 99.0% of deep suppression, and Subgroup-Covariate-Weighted conformal risk control bounded all 70 TIVA shift cells at ≤4.38% (alpha=5.0%) in 66.32 ms per 30-s epoch.

papers.title: Increased temporal persistence of reference-invariant bilateral EEG states in adult ADHD.
papers.summary: Compared resting EEG from 56 adults with ADHD and 179 healthy adults to test the temporal persistence of bilateral relational states across 10 homologous pairs and four frequency bands, with eyes-closed discovery and eyes-open generalization. Only four reference-invariant bipolar-envelope targets (Fp1-Fp2 theta and beta, C3-C4 delta, P3-P4 delta) were significant in the same direction in both conditions and under age adjustment, while broad sensor-envelope effects did not survive common-average re-referencing.

papers.title: NeuroSim: a clinically informed multi-disorder EEG simulator with personalized pattern injection and AI-driven neurological modeling
papers.summary: Presents NeuroSim, an open-source framework generating synthetic multichannel EEG with user-controlled injection of disease-specific spectral patterns across five disorders and severity levels, reproducing expected biomarkers. A convolutional-attention classifier trained on simulated data reached 95.3–96.8% hold-out accuracy, and augmenting real clinical EEG with NeuroSim samples improved AD vs. control accuracy from 91.6% to 94.5% and PD vs. control from 90.9% to 94.0%.

papers.title: SafeLens: A Statistically Controlled Nonlinear Machine Learning Framework for Characterizing Hidden Dynamics in Event-Locked Neural Activity.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces SafeLens, a sliding-window random-forest framework with empirical null sampling that maps nonlinear reliance on multiscale temporal derivatives across time-frequency space while controlling family-wise error. On simulated cortico-cortical evoked potentials injected into resting intracranial EEG, it recovered ~2.5 times more polarity-resolved deflections with ~5–11 times fewer false components, and in eight patients detected CCEPs until 1,040 ms post-stimulation versus 570 and 455 ms for benchmarks.

papers.title: Seizure Prediction Using Channel-Optimized Intracranial EEG With Variable Interictal and Preictal Durations.
papers.journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
papers.summary: Evaluated seizure prediction on long-term SWEC-ETHZ intracranial EEG across six interictal (24/48 h) and preictal (30/60/90 min) duration combinations, comparing all-channel, single-channel majority voting, and channel-optimization majority voting strategies. Channel optimization performed best in every combination, reaching up to 87.7% sensitivity, 94.6% specificity, 0.912 AUC at the segment level and 95.9% sensitivity with 0.05/h FPR at the event level, forecasting seizures up to 90 min ahead.

papers.title: A shared slowing axis and phenotype-specific rhythms link clinical EEG to FDG-PET dementia phenotypes.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Applied nonnegative tensor decomposition to clinical EEG in 455 patients, deriving six latent factors and relating them to FDG-PET-defined neurodegenerative phenotypes, regional metabolism, and cognition. Four oscillatory factors (posterior alpha, Rolandic beta, frontotemporal delta-theta, posterior theta-slow alpha) varied across phenotypes, with posterior theta-slow alpha becoming more phenotype-specific after slowing adjustment (eta-squared 0.082 to 0.147), and a four-factor logistic classifier separated cognitively unimpaired participants from DLB, posterior cortical atrophy, and AD variants with AUC > 0.8.

papers.title: Reading Across Space, Time and Frequencies: Tensor Decomposition of SEEG Signals to Support Epileptogenic Zone Definition
papers.summary: Proposes a Canonical Polyadic decomposition framework modeling SEEG signals as a channel × time × frequency tensor to extract latent modes underlying seizure generation, using channel-specific factors as unsupervised features for epileptogenic zone identification. Validated on SEEG-recorded seizures from 35 drug-resistant epilepsy patients, the results show that jointly combining multiple frequency bands significantly enhances classification performance.

papers.title: FUSE: FUsing EEG-MEG in a Shared Embedding via self-supervised learning for BCI
papers.summary: Introduces FUSE, a two-phase self-supervised framework that learns a shared EEG-MEG latent representation by predicting power spectral density from time-domain activity and then reuses the frozen encoder for motor imagery BCI classification. On simultaneous EEG-MEG from 20 participants, the learned representations raised median accuracy from 0.734 with handcrafted spectral features to 0.794, also outperforming MEG alone (0.680) and slightly EEG alone (0.765), with cross-subject transfer within 0.01 accuracy for over half of models.

papers.title: The Potency Stability Tradeoff: Evaluating EEG Biomarkers for Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.summary: Deconstructed EEG-based MDD biomarkers using connectivity, spectral, and complexity features from 30 MDD patients and 88 controls under leakage-free cross-validation, finding Theta-Alpha signals maximally predictive (AUC 0.683) but unstable (Jaccard 0.187), while stability-optimized consensus feature selection gave superior generalization (AUC 0.792 vs 0.662). Concludes biomarker stability matters more than signal strength for clinically reliable diagnostics.

papers.title: Predicting Alzheimer progression using EEG-based digital twins.
papers.summary: Evaluated the Digital Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis (DADD) digital twin framework, which maps EEG-derived digital biomarkers to latent parameters of AD mechanisms, in 459 participants with SCD or MCI over 10-year follow-up. Digital biomarkers predicted conversion risk and timing, matched established APOE/MRI/CSF biomarkers, outperformed them in SCD, and improved prognostic accuracy when combined with them.

papers.title: Transition Dynamics Matter: Hidden Markov Scoring of Epileptogenic Channels in SEEG
papers.summary: Proposed a joint Hidden Markov Model in which each SEEG channel has a latent chain sharing states across the network with channel-specific transition probabilities, using KL divergence between inter-ictal and seizure-onset transition probabilities to identify epileptogenic-zone channels. In 30 drug-resistant epilepsy patients, modeling channel-specific temporal transitions improved EZ localization versus a latent-state-free benchmark.

papers.title: Frontotemporal Slow-Frequency Dominance in Quantitative EEG as a Potential Biomarker of Post-COVID Cognitive Dysfunction.
authors: María Mar González Álvarez de Sotomayor
papers.summary: Exploratory case-control qEEG study of 21 patients with persistent cognitive complaints after mild COVID-19 versus 21 matched controls found a spatially heterogeneous shift toward slower spectral activity, most consistent in frontal and right temporal electrodes, with modest cognitive associations and exploratory classification performance (ROC-AUC up to 0.949). Findings require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

papers.title: Next generation Human Neocortical Neurosolver model with biophysically realistic somatic, dendritic and synaptic dynamics.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Presents a significantly updated Human Neocortical Neurosolver model with electrophysiological properties and synaptic connections tuned to human tissue, including L5 dendritic Ca2+ spikes and shorter L2/3 dendritic spikes, plus software workflows and tutorials for disentangling somatic, synaptic, and dendritic contributions to EEG/MEG signatures.

papers.title: A report-supervised EEG-language foundation model enables broad, interactive clinical interpretation
papers.summary: Introduces EEG Copilot, a biosignal-language foundation model trained on routine EEG-report pairs without task-specific expert labels. Across external datasets it matched an expert-supervised model on 11 findings (mean AUROC 0.80–0.81), assessed 23 clinical characteristics via natural-language queries in English and German, and produced clinically usable integrated impressions.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG features of cognitive fluctuations across the Lewy body disease spectrum.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 53 Lewy body disease patients, resting-state EEG features (dominant frequency, dominant frequency prevalence-alpha, individual alpha peak frequency) were significantly lower in those with cognitive fluctuations and predicted group membership after adjustment for age, sex, and MoCA (AUC 0.85-0.86). The authors propose these EEG features as a potential biomarker to improve diagnosis of Lewy body dementia.

papers.title: Prediction of surgical outcome using cyclic spectral coherent networks of intracranial EEG signals.
papers.summary: Proposes a cyclostationary-based connectivity framework using Cyclic Spectral Coherence on intracranial EEG to identify network hubs and compute a Resection Hub Alignment Degree (RHAD) metric. Preictal RHAD-EVC differentiated seizure-free (Engel I) from non-seizure-free patients (p < 0.01) with an AUC of 0.64 for surgical outcome prediction.

papers.title: False-Positive Calls of Reimplemented Published Analyses for Covert Command-Following on Electroencephalograms Recorded Without Study Commands.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Applied 11 reimplemented published EEG analyses for covert command-following to recordings made without commands across large clinical cohorts, measuring false-positive rates. Three of ten analyses called significantly more than 5% of patients positive (up to 23.3%, and 11.5–27.3% after cardiac arrest) while still detecting genuine responses, and the authors identify variance handling, configuration/time selection, and permissive thresholds as contributors.

papers.title: Neural Entropy Pattern : An EEG Representation for Predicting Depression Therapy Outcomes.
papers.summary: Introduces the Neural Entropy Pattern (NEP), a 20×57 EEG representation of ten entropy measures across 19 channels and five frequency bands, tested with deep and shallow classifiers to predict antidepressant (SSRI) and rTMS response. Best balanced accuracy was 76.4% (AUC 0.89) for SSRI under leave-one-subject-out and 62.1–63.7% for rTMS, with log-energy and differential entropy carrying most importance and F7/T3 features dominating SSRI prediction.

papers.title: Behavioral Latency as Weak Event-Time Supervision for EEG Reaction-Time Decoding.
papers.summary: Reformulates single-trial EEG reaction-time decoding as event-time posterior modeling, estimating p(t_event|X) with posterior mean as the RT estimate and treating behavioral latency as weak supervision. Across five seeds on the Healthy Brain Network contrast-change task, distributional event-time supervision improved held-out RT prediction over scalar regression and temporal-readout controls across four temporal backbones.

papers.title: Cross-Attention Estimation of Asynchronous EEG Functional Networks for Affective Disorder Characterization.
papers.summary: Proposes an attention-based causal-discovery framework (CACD) for interpretable asynchronous EEG functional networks that jointly estimates directed influence strength, transmission delay, and modulation sign using a dual-branch decoder, learnable cross-attention mask, and attention-gradient consistency. CACD recovered causal structures and delays on nine benchmarks and achieved competitive subject-independent affective-disorder classification on three clinical EEG datasets, with delay and modulation adding discriminative value beyond directed influence.

papers.title: Tracking Neurophysiological Trajectories in Adolescent Non-Suicidal Self-Injury During Mindfulness-Based Intervention: A Longitudinal Single-Channel EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a prospective longitudinal observational study of 52 hospitalized adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury undergoing home-based EEG biofeedback meditation, exploratory responders showed progressive increases in single-channel alpha/beta ratio that were positively associated with total mood disturbance improvement (r=0.43). The authors conclude that EEG trajectory analysis may be a promising objective monitoring approach, though a control group was lacking.

papers.title: Temporal Contrastive Alignment of EEG and Naturalistic Video Only Beats Linear Decoding On In-Sample Stimuli
papers.summary: A temporal contrastive model pairing pretrained VideoMAE features with a lightweight EEG encoder (correlation-based InfoNCE) was benchmarked against CCA for EEG-video alignment; it outperformed CCA in leave-one-subject-out and matched it in leave-video-segment-out, but fell behind on novel videos, and a sham control showed high accuracy can occur without genuine temporal alignment. On attention decoding with seen stimuli the model still exceeded CCA, and group-averaged EEG revealed genuine generalizable coupling buried in single-subject noise.

papers.title: A Soft Sponge-Pillar Electrode Platform for Motion-Tolerant Ambulatory EEG and Sleep Monitoring.
papers.summary: A soft sponge-pillar EEG electrode of two-layer carbon black-PDMS composite, fabricated by sugar templating, was developed for motion-tolerant ambulatory recording, achieving contact impedance of 1.62×10^4 Ω at 10 Hz and maintaining gel stability over 18 hours. Integrated into headbands, headphones, and caps, it recorded EEG during motion with 16.46 dB SNR, supporting wearable long-term EEG and sleep monitoring.

papers.title: Group-specific associations among sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and frontal alpha asymmetry in college students: evidence from a cross-sectional EEG study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 120 college students (60 with elevated depressive symptoms, 60 controls), the depressive-symptom group had higher PSQI scores and lower composite frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA). PSQI correlated positively with depressive symptoms in both groups, while FAA correlated negatively with PSQI and depressive symptoms only in the depressive-symptom group, where PSQI and FAA jointly explained depressive symptom severity (R²=0.243).

papers.title: Characterizing source-level electroencephalography activities to single-pulse TMS-EEG.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Thirty-three healthy adults underwent active and sham single-pulse TMS-EEG over left DLPFC, with source-level significant current density (SCD) and scattering (SCS) analyzed; active stimulation produced larger early local TEPs (2.15±1.39 vs 0.85±0.66 μV) and greater target-region SCS and SCD in both early and late windows. Whole-brain significant clusters appeared only at late latencies (e.g., SCS 275-333 ms), and one SCD cluster lost significance after muscle-related adjustment.

papers.title: Electrophysiology of multisite direct electrical stimulation in the human brain.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In 20 participants with stereo-EEG, simultaneous multisite direct electrical stimulation showed that synchronized dual-site stimulation engaged a larger effective network than single-site stimulation; linear superposition explained most responses, with sublinear (saturation) responses proximal to stimulation sites and supralinear late responses at network-connected sites. Low-intensity dual-site stimulation matched or exceeded higher-intensity single-site stimulation, and these principles extended to three-site stimulation.

papers.title: Routine greenery encounters and anxiety occurrence probability: a study of component contributions in university residential greenery scenes based on mobile electroencephalography data.
papers.summary: This exploratory study related mobile EEG-derived Anxiety Occurrence Probability (frontal alpha asymmetry, theta/beta ratio) to 13 quantified greenery components along a 45-m campus route in 35 university students. Color richness, shading rate, green view ratio, and visibility were negatively associated with AOP (model adjusted R² = 0.770), with piecewise breakpoints of 0.321 for shading rate and 0.451 for visibility; findings are correlational.

papers.title: Frontal Low-Frequency Electroencephalographic Coherence in Bipolar Disorder: A Covariate-Controlled Secondary Analysis of a Public Resting-State EEG Feature Dataset.
papers.summary: In a covariate-controlled secondary analysis of a public resting-state EEG dataset (93 healthy controls, 66 bipolar disorder, 196 depressive disorder, 117 schizophrenia), bipolar disorder showed higher adjusted frontal/frontopolar delta, theta, and combined delta-theta coherence than all comparison groups, with effects strongest in frontopolar electrode pairs. Differences from depressive disorder and schizophrenia were smaller and concentrated in frontopolar pairs susceptible to ocular artifacts, so the findings do not establish a diagnostic biomarker or source-level mechanism.

papers.title: Depressive symptoms moderate daily anticipated and momentary emotion dynamics and associate with complex brain network topology: Resting-state EEG and ecological momentary assessment evidence.
papers.summary: Combining resting-state EEG minimum spanning tree analysis with 14-day ecological momentary assessment (3 assessments/day) in 96 young adults, the study found anticipated emotion prospectively predicted subsequent momentary positive and negative emotion, but this link attenuated to non-significance beyond PHQ-9 scores of 5.7-9.7. Theta- and delta-band topological metrics were indirectly associated with daily emotional dynamics via baseline depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Supraorbital Near-Infrared Stimulation and Portable EEG: An Exploratory Fixed-Order Study of Spectral Markers and Signal Quality.
papers.summary: In a fixed-order exploratory study of 25 healthy women, global gamma log-power change during bilateral 940-nm supraorbital near-infrared stimulation differed from sham (mean difference-in-change 0.101 a.u., Cohen's dz = 0.43, paired t-test p = 0.040), but Wilcoxon inference was non-significant (p = 0.090) and signal quality differed between visits. The authors conclude that visit-order confounding and unverified signal origin preclude conclusions about stimulation effects or cortical gamma modulation.

papers.title: Changes in negative affect and resting-state EEG power following an EEG-derived generative reality art experience: a pilot pre-post study.
papers.summary: This single-group pilot pre-post study exposed 30 healthy students to a 5-min EEG-derived generative VR art experience and measured affect and resting-state EEG. Negative affect decreased (mean change -3.13) and absolute alpha/beta power decreased in frontal, frontocentral, and central regions, but EEG changes were not associated with affect changes and no neural mechanism or causality was established.

papers.title: Epilepsy Surgery in Patients with Non-Lesional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Evaluated with Stereoelectroencephalography: Retrospective Analysis in a High-Complexity Center and Literature Review.
papers.summary: This retrospective series of 11 patients with non-lesional MRI epilepsy evaluated with stereoelectroencephalography reported successful epileptogenic zone hypotheses in all patients and a 63.6% rate of good postoperative (Engel) outcomes, with anterior temporal lobectomy in four and extratemporal corticectomy in seven. Unlike prior studies, the authors' extratemporal non-lesional subgroup showed better postoperative results than the temporal subgroup.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for infrared spectral analysis of bone.
papers.summary: Using optical photothermal infrared spectroscopy of wild-type and osteogenesis imperfecta mouse bone, full-spectrum fingerprint-region (1800-800 cm-1) models reached 87-90% phenotype classification accuracy versus 59-63% for conventional peak-ratio parameters, with similar performance across PLS-DA, logistic regression, and XGBoost. SHAP and VIP identified prominent contributions from collagen-associated Amide I and II regions.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN: Identifying Phelan-McDermid-Like Electrophysiological Subtypes in Autism Using EEG and Machine Learning
papers.summary: This manuscript was withdrawn by the authors pending re-evaluation of the clinical data, and they request it not be cited; no findings are reported in the available abstract.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
